patients.summary: Healthy administrative assistant who joins the practice at 23 in 2021 for routine prevention. Contraceptive counseling in late 2024, a Bartholin's gland cyst seen by gynecology in 2025, and in March 2026, after her last practice visit, an admission elsewhere for disseminated gonococcal infection treated with ceftriaxone.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
23 yo woman establishing care. Moved to Easthampton last year for work, admin assistant at an office in town. Feels well, no complaints today. Wants a physical and to get set up.

PMH: none. Never hospitalized. No surgeries.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: none to medications.
Gyn: menses regular, monthly. G0. No history of STIs. Last Pap at her old office in 2019, she recalls it was fine. Thinks she had the HPV shots in middle school.
FH: nothing she knows of that runs in the family.
SH: never a smoker, does not drink, no recreational drugs. Lives alone. Walks most evenings.
Vaccines: two Pfizer COVID doses this spring at a pharmacy clinic (April). Unsure about last tetanus.

ROS negative across systems.

Exam: Vitals as charted, BMI in normal range. Well appearing. HEENT unremarkable, thyroid not enlarged. Cardiac exam regular rhythm, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without lesions. No edema. Mood and affect appropriate.

Plan:
1. Health maintenance. Screening labs today: CBC, CMP. One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening, she agrees. Urine chlamydia/gonorrhea screen given age. PHQ-2 is 0.
2. Tdap given today (no record of a booster since childhood).
3. Records request to her prior PCP for the Pap and vaccine history. Pap next year if 2019 result confirmed normal.
4. Return in a year for a physical, sooner as needed. She knows she can text the office.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Christine, everything from Tuesday came back normal. Blood count, kidney and liver tests are all fine, and the HIV, hepatitis C, chlamydia and gonorrhea screens were all negative. Nothing to do. Good to meet you.

documents.title: Office Visit - Contraception
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to talk about birth control. About two months into a new relationship, having sex with this partner, and they haven't been using anything reliably. She wants to avoid pregnancy and is also worried about infections since she doesn't know his testing history.

Cycles regular. LMP roughly two weeks ago. Never pregnant. No prior STI. No meds, NKDA. FH noncontributory. Doesn't smoke, drink or use drugs.
GU ROS: no discharge, no pelvic pain, no burning with urination.

Exam: vitals as charted. Pelvic exam with chaperone: external genitalia normal, vaginal walls and cervix normal, no discharge, no cervical motion tenderness, uterus and adnexa normal size and nontender. Swabs collected.

Assessment and plan: Contraceptive counseling. Went through the options: pill, patch, ring, injection, implant and IUDs, plus condoms. Explained that only condoms also lower STI risk, and that pairing condoms with a second method is the most protective against pregnancy. She prefers to start with condoms alone for now and use them every time; open to adding a hormonal method later. Encouraged her partner to get tested. Gave information on emergency contraception available over the counter.
GC/CT NAAT sent today.
Return any time to revisit.

documents.title: Test results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Christine, chlamydia and gonorrhea were both negative. Let me know if you'd like to talk about adding another method.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Painless swelling near the vaginal opening, first felt in the shower about two months ago, slowly larger since. No pain, bleeding or drainage. No fever, no dysuria. Still using condoms with the same partner.

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. Chaperone present. Soft, smooth swelling at the lower vestibule beside the introitus, not tender, skin over it normal, no redness. No other vulvar lesions.

Assessment: most consistent with a Bartholin gland cyst.
Plan: reviewed that these are common and often left alone when painless. Given it has been growing, referring to gynecology to confirm and advise. Warm soaks if it becomes sore; call right away for pain, redness or fever.

documents.title: Gynecology Consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY - CONSULTATION LETTER
Date of service: 03/11/2025
Reason for referral: vulvar swelling, from primary care

Thank you for sending this 27-year-old. Three months ago she first felt a lump at the vaginal opening while showering. It has grown slowly. She has had no pain, no bleeding and no drainage from it, and denies fever, urinary burning or feeling unwell. Primary care counseled her on contraception in December.

Allergies: NKDA. Medications: none. Family history: noncontributory.
Sexual history: one male partner; condom use is not consistent.

Examination: At the posterior vestibule, lateral to the vaginal orifice, there is a 3 cm soft, fluctuant mass that is not tender. The mucosa over it is intact without redness or induration. Labia majora and minora otherwise without lesions. No inguinal adenopathy. Vagina, cervix, uterus and adnexa normal on the rest of the pelvic exam.

Impression: Bartholin's gland cyst, asymptomatic.

Recommendations: No drainage or procedure is needed for a painless cyst at her age. Warm sitz baths if it becomes uncomfortable. She should return or contact primary care if it becomes painful, red, rapidly larger, or drains. Happy to see her again as needed.

Outside obstetrics and gynecology

documents.title: Gynecology visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Christine, I got the gynecology letter. They agree it's a Bartholin cyst and that nothing needs to be done while it isn't bothering you. Sitz baths if it gets uncomfortable, and let us know if it becomes painful or red.

documents.title: RE: Gynecology visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks, that's what she told me too. Relieved!

events.reason: fever, painful swollen right knee, pustular skin lesions

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
COMMUNITY HOSPITAL - EMERGENCY SERVICES
Arrival 03/03/2026 10:40

CC: fever x3 days, R knee pain and swelling, spots on arms and legs

HPI: 28F, previously healthy, history of a Bartholin's gland cyst and past contraceptive counseling with her PCP. Three days of fevers with aching in several joints, now mostly the right knee, which is swollen and hurts enough that she is limping. Noticed several small pus-filled bumps on her arms and legs. No fall or injury.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA. FH noncontributory.
Social: sexual activity with more than one partner recently; condoms not used every time.

Triage: T 38.7 C (101.7 F), HR 102, BP 120/78.

Exam: febrile, uncomfortable. R knee swollen, red, warm and tender with limited flexion and extension. Scattered small pustules on the extremities. No urethral discharge.

Procedure: R knee arthrocentesis under sterile technique, fluid sent for cell count, Gram stain and culture. Tolerated well.

Results: WBC 12.0 K/uL. ESR 50 mm/hr. CRP 25 mg/L. Synovial fluid WBC 25,000/uL, 90% neutrophils; Gram stain without organisms. Blood cultures drawn x2. Urine NAAT for gonorrhea sent, pending at time of admission.

MDM: febrile inflammatory monoarthritis with pustular skin lesions and polyarthralgia in a sexually active young woman; disseminated gonococcal infection is the leading concern, septic arthritis of the knee on the differential. Ceftriaxone 1 g IV given after cultures. Admitted to medicine.

Disposition: admitted.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
COMMUNITY HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 03/03/2026 via the ED. Discharged 03/09/2026.

Discharge diagnosis: disseminated gonococcal infection with right knee arthritis and pustular skin lesions.
Other: high-risk sexual behavior (multiple partners, inconsistent condom use).

Hospital course: 28-year-old woman admitted with three days of fever, polyarthralgia, an inflamed right knee and pustules on the extremities. Knee aspirate in the ED was inflammatory (25,000 WBC/uL, 90% neutrophils) with a negative Gram stain. Started on ceftriaxone 1 g IV every 24 hours. Urine gonorrhea NAAT returned positive on 03/04; chlamydia NAAT negative. Urine pregnancy test negative. HIV antigen/antibody and RPR nonreactive. Blood cultures no growth at 5 days and synovial fluid culture no growth. Fever resolved by the second hospital day. Knee swelling and pain steadily improved and she was walking comfortably by discharge. Skin lesions faded. She completed a 7-day course of ceftriaxone before discharge. Acetaminophen as needed for discomfort.

Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge medications: acetaminophen 1000 mg by mouth every 6 hours as needed. No antibiotics at discharge; course complete.

Counseling: all partners from the past 60 days should be told, tested and treated; patient given partner notification information. No sexual contact until 7 days after her treatment and until partners are treated. Condoms with every partner.

Follow-up: primary care in 1 to 2 weeks. Repeat gonorrhea testing in 3 months.

Hospital medicine service
